title: Implement liveness probes that detect unrecoverable local failure
description: Use a liveness probe only when restarting the container can resolve a failure. Avoid coupling liveness to a shared downstream dependency, which can trigger restart storms during an outage. Test thresholds under load.

documentation.title: Implement liveness probes that detect unrecoverable local failure

title: Protect slow startup with a startup probe
description: Configure a startup probe with a failure budget covering the measured worst-case startup. Liveness and readiness probes do not run until the startup probe succeeds; test image pulls and cold initialization separately.

documentation.title: Protect slow startup with a startup probe

title: Implement a proper Readiness probe
description: Sometimes, applications are temporarily unable to serve traffic. For example, an application might need to load large data or configuration files during startup, or depend on external services after startup. In such cases, you don't want to kill the application, but you don't want to send it requests either. Kubernetes provides readiness probes to detect and mitigate these situations. A pod with containers reporting that they are not ready does not receive traffic through Kubernetes Services.

documentation.title: Configure Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes

title: Implement graceful termination and connection draining
description: Handle termination signals, configure terminationGracePeriodSeconds, and use preStop only where needed. Allow in-flight requests to drain and test rolling updates and node drains. Hooks are not guaranteed during every failure, so persist critical state safely.

documentation.title: Implement graceful termination and connection draining

title: Run enough replicas for the availability target
description: Use multiple replicas for services that require high availability, and spread them across nodes and zones. Test that the remaining replicas can serve peak demand during failure or maintenance; replica count alone does not establish resilience.

documentation.title: Pod replicas

title: Apply tags/labels to all resources
description: Ensure that your components are tagged, it could be business, security or technical tags and these tags will help to assess or apply relevant policies.

documentation.title: Recommended Labels

title: Autoscale applications using measured demand
description: Configure HPA or KEDA with appropriate metrics, requests, replica bounds, and stabilization windows. Test metric outages, burst traffic, dependency limits, and scale-down; ensure node scaling and regional capacity can satisfy demand.

documentation.title: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler

title: Keep secrets out of images and use a managed secret store
description: Store application secrets in Key Vault and retrieve them with a supported integration and least-privilege identity. AKS provides encryption at rest, but Kubernetes Secrets are still accessible to authorized API clients and are not an external vault. Never commit secrets to source or bake them into images.

documentation.title: Keep secrets out of images and use a managed secret store

title: Use Microsoft Entra Workload ID for application access
description: Enable the OIDC issuer and Workload ID, then federate a dedicated Kubernetes service account to a least-privilege managed identity. Use supported SDKs and the required workload identity label. Replace the retired pod-managed identity add-on; do not give applications node identity permissions.

documentation.title: Use Microsoft Entra Workload ID for application access

title: Use namespaces with explicit access and policy boundaries
description: Use dedicated namespaces for workloads and apply scoped RBAC, quotas, and network/admission policy. Avoid deploying applications into default or system namespaces. Namespaces provide logical separation, not a complete security boundary.

documentation.title: Namespaces

title: Set up requests and limits on your containers
description: When Containers have resource requests specified, the scheduler can make better decisions about which nodes to place Pods on. And when Containers have their limits specified, contention for resources on a node can be handled in a specified manner.

documentation.title: Managing Compute Resources for Containers
Take benefit of the Quality of Service

title: Declare an explicit workload security context
description: Use platform-appropriate least-privilege settings. For Linux, prefer non-root, RuntimeDefault seccomp, dropped capabilities, no privilege escalation, and a read-only root filesystem. Disable automatic service account token mounting where the workload does not need it; validate projected tokens required by Workload ID.

documentation.title: Declare an explicit workload security context

title: Ensure your manifests respect good practices
description: Best practices inside the cluster start with the configuration of your manifests. Ensure that they respect good practices

documentation.title: Kubernetes application security checklist

title: Lint Dockerfiles and enforce an image-build baseline
description: Validate base-image provenance, pinned versions, non-root execution where supported, build secrets, dependency installation, and unnecessary packages. Use maintained linters and policy checks without exposing build credentials in layers or logs.

documentation.title: SNYK 10 Docker Image Security Best Practices
21 Best Practises in 2021 for Dockerfile

title: Scan container images during the build
description: Scan OS packages and application dependencies during image builds with maintained tools. Retain reports linked to immutable digests, define remediation targets, and rescan deployed versions as new vulnerabilities are disclosed.

documentation.title: Container vulnerability assessment

title: Enforce image vulnerability thresholds and exception expiry
description: Define policy using exploitability, exposure, severity, and available fixes. Block unacceptable risk, record owners and expiry for exceptions, and rescan continuously. An unfixed critical vulnerability is not automatically acceptable simply because the vendor has not published a fix.

documentation.title: Enforce image vulnerability thresholds and exception expiry

title: Validate container build and runtime policy
description: Validate approved base images, non-root execution where supported, exposed services, secret handling, and required labels. Apply rules based on the threat model; opening port 80 alone is not proof of noncompliance.

documentation.title: Validate container build and runtime policy

title: Assess application modernization before containerization
description: Validate runtime support, licensing, state, external dependencies, health probes, and operational ownership before moving an application to AKS. Choose supported migration tooling based on the workload rather than assuming a point-and-containerize conversion produces a production-ready service.

documentation.title: Assess application modernization before containerization

title: Apply the right deployment type to your application
description: There are a variety of techniques to deploy new applications to production so choosing the right strategy is an important decision that needs to be made to leverage the impact of change on the consumer.

documentation.title: Kubernetes Deployment Strategies

title: Use workload controllers instead of standalone pods
description: Manage long-running applications through Deployments or StatefulSets, and finite work through Jobs or CronJobs. A standalone pod is not recreated after node loss by a workload controller; test replacement and application recovery.
details: If imagePullPolicy is omitted and either the image tag is :latest or it is omitted: imagePullPolicy is automatically set to Always. Prefer to set explicitly IfNotPresent

documentation.title: Use workload controllers instead of standalone pods

title: Set image pull policy and deploy immutable image digests
description: Use immutable digests for reproducible deployments and choose imagePullPolicy deliberately. Always checks registry resolution but can reuse cached layers; IfNotPresent reuses cached images. Do not rely on mutable latest tags, and test registry failure behavior.

documentation.title: Set image pull policy and deploy immutable image digests

title: Provision Azure resources with reviewed infrastructure as code
description: Use Bicep, ARM templates, or Terraform modules with pinned versions, environment-specific configuration, least-privilege deployment identities, and reviewed changes. Keep state protected, detect drift, and rehearse rebuilding the platform.

documentation.title: Provision Azure resources with reviewed infrastructure as code

title: Use canary or blue/green deployments
description: This will help ensure your workloads remain online during cluster upgrades.

documentation.title: Blue-green deployment for AKS

title: Evaluate Dapr only when its application capabilities are needed
description: Dapr can provide service invocation, pub/sub, state management, and other distributed application APIs. Adopt it when those capabilities justify additional sidecars, control-plane components, security configuration, and lifecycle management; it is not an upgrade-availability mechanism.

documentation.title: Evaluate Dapr only when its application capabilities are needed

title: Validate deprecated Kubernetes APIs before every upgrade
description: Check release notes, API-server warnings, manifests, CRDs, Helm charts, operators, and admission webhooks for APIs removed in the target version. Upgrade dependencies first and test conversion and rollback paths in a representative environment.

documentation.title: Validate deprecated Kubernetes APIs before every upgrade

title: Secure CI/CD with federation and scoped deployment permissions
description: Use OIDC federation from the CI platform to Azure, protect release environments, pin reviewed actions and build dependencies, and scope deployment identities to the required namespaces and resources. Keep production credentials and kubeconfig files out of logs and artifacts.

documentation.title: Secure CI/CD with federation and scoped deployment permissions
